title: Seasonal cross-spectrum surrogates rarely matched six-month Nino 3.4 change asymmetry in 1950-2025
abstract: We tested a selected six-month change imbalance in NOAA CPC ERSSTv5 Nino 3.4 for 1950-2025. The observed normalized cubic change statistic was -0.5066. We treated calendar months as 12 channels in a 76-year vector series. Among 999 surrogates with exact month distributions and approximate annual cross spectra, one had an absolute statistic at least this large. The nominal tail fraction was 0.002. Median relative cross-spectrum error was 8.75%. A comparison with exact cross spectra but no rank matching gave a fraction of 0.018. Neither ensemble reduced to nearly exact circular year shifts. A stationary rank control gave 0.003. This adds seasonal covariance constraints to prior distribution and autoregressive checks on the same record. It is not independent confirmation or a calibrated rejection of all seasonal linear models. Spectral fit error, circular endpoints, prior selection, source uncertainty and constrained sampling limit interpretation. The package contains original code, aggregate simulation evidence, source hashes, an audit and a figure. External monthly records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Observed six-month cubic change statistic and central 95% ranges from three surrogate ensembles in 1950-2025. Ranges describe surrogate outputs, not uncertainty in the observed statistic. Seasonal rank error is cross-spectrum error; scalar rank error is amplitude error.
